# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | blue |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My situation: I hold the only reliable truth — the manual. Blue light → cut green, green light → cut blue, red light → cut red, and the manual always beats whatever the bomb prints or makes us feel. But I cannot speak a word of it, and my gestures reach exactly one monkey: Deaf. The Blind can only hear speech, so every fact I hold has to travel me → gesture → Deaf → speech → Blind. Deaf is my only bridge.

The problem: gestures mean nothing yet. I can't explain the table, I can only build a code. The one convention that needs no explanation is 👍 for yes and 👎 for no. So my opening move is to offer Deaf a question-and-answer channel: I greet, I signal "ask me", and I present the two answer symbols. Once Deaf catches on, they can look at the bomb, see the light's colour and the wires' colours and order, ask me enumerated questions — and crucially, in the same breath describe the bomb aloud to the Blind, who hears everything Deaf says.

I expect Deaf to ask, and next round I'll answer each question in order with a sequence of 👍/👎. The mapping is small: at most three rows, and the light colour they need is the one Deaf can already see. I should also make sure, through this channel, that the bomb's own printed claims get distrusted — the manual wins over the bomb — but that can be confirmed once the yes/no channel is live.

For now: open the channel.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤌", "👍", "👎", "🙏"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | blue |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Touch report: there is an embossed sign that reads DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. I feel three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, but I cannot feel their colours. There is also a display and a light; I can feel both parts but cannot read the display or tell whether the light is on. Deaf sees the bomb and can say the colours, the display and the light out loud, and both of us will hear it. Remember: my voice reaches only you, and your gestures never reach me, so the only way your manual answer gets to me is through Deaf's voice. Please look up this module, especially what DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE means, and sign the rule to Deaf so Deaf can speak it to me. Nobody cuts until we have it.
Deaf says: Bomb report from my eyes: the display reads zero. One indicator light is lit, colour blue. An embossed plate reads: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Three wires, left to right: wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. That is everything I can see. Nobody cuts any wire unless Mute's manual, relayed through me, clearly orders it. I will report any change to the display or light every round.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received your five gestures, but we had no shared code yet, so they were unreadable to me. Let us fix one now. Numbers, as named hand signs: raised fist is zero. Index finger up is one. Victory two. Love-you sign three. Crossed fingers four. Five fingers spread five. Call-me hand six. Horns seven. Vulcan salute eight. Pinched fingers nine. Thumbs up means yes. Thumbs down means no. Folded hands means question, or please repeat. Waving hand means attention. Colours: oncoming fist is red. Raised palm is green. Back of raised hand is blue. Actions: pointing down is cut. Pointing up is press. Flat palm down is release. Flat palm up is hold. Clap means done. Point left means wire one, leftmost. Point right means wire three, rightmost. Send me facts as chains: wire number, then colour, then action. If your manual numbers its sections or instructions, we can refer to them by those number signs. If you accept this code, send thumbs up, then answer three questions, one gesture each, in this order: one, does the manual mention a blue light? Two, does it mention a display showing zero? Three, does it mention a plate saying do not cut any wire? Thumbs up or thumbs down for each.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👍 👎 🙏]

What I know: the manual is the only always-true source, and its table is the way out — blue light → cut green, green → blue, red → red. Deaf reports the light is blue, so the truth is: cut the green wire, which is wire 2. The embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE plate and the zero display are the bomb's print — the manual explicitly says the bomb may mislead and that the only way out is the cut, so both are to be ignored; my answers to Deaf's questions (yes / no / no) make that clear, since the manual mentions neither.

Deaf built a complete code and asked for acceptance plus three answers. That code is my only bridge to Blind, so I accept it and immediately pack everything into one ordered stream Deaf can read aloud in full: attention, code accepted, yes–no–no to the three questions, then the operative order cut-green, a separator, and the entire manual table encoded as three colour-cut-colour rules so that even if the light changes, Deaf and Blind can act without waiting another round for me. Clap ends it — that is the whole manual, nothing held back.

Everything must live in one gesture stream: I have no speech, and my gestures reach Deaf alone, so Deaf's voice is the sole channel to Blind. Deaf has already committed to relaying verbatim and to no cutting without my manual's order — this stream is that order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👇", "🖐", "👋", "✋", "👇", "🖐", "🖐", "👇", "✋", "✊", "👇", "✊", "👏"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | blue |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile sweep complete, every part checked: the bomb holds exactly four things under my hands — the display, the indicator light, the embossed plate reading DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and three wires in a row at positions 1, 2 and 3. There are no buttons, no switches, no panels, no flaps, nothing else anywhere on it. So the whole puzzle is what Deaf reported: display zero, blue light lit, that warning plate, and wires red, green, blue. I have confirmed to Deaf by thumbs up that my earlier gesture meant the three wires. Please look up this module now and give a clear verdict to Deaf to speak aloud: does the plate mean no wire may ever be cut, or is there a condition such as the display reading zero or the blue light that tells us which wire to cut or that we must do nothing? Until your answer comes back through Deaf, nobody touches the cutters.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I decoded your opening: wave, then code accepted, blue light yes, display zero no, plate no. If I read that right, hold that thought. Your tail after it was garbled, my fault: I left green with two possible hand signs, and zero and red were two similar fists, so I could not trust what you sent. Fixed code, one meaning per hand, use only these. Colours: red is oncoming fist only, green is raised hand only, blue is back of hand only. The spread five hand is only the number five, never a colour. The raised fist is only zero, never red. Resend your tail as strict chains: wire number, then colour, then action, and place a wave between different instructions. Example: two, green, cut. After you resend I will echo my reading back and you correct me with thumbs only. If chaining is difficult, just send a wave then three thumbs, one each, in this order: one, does the manual tell us to cut any wire on this bomb; two, does the manual rule depend on the light being blue; three, does the manual instruct any action other than cutting, such as press, hold, or a switch. Status from my eyes this round: no change, display zero, light blue, wires red green blue.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 🙏]

The critical fact is confirmed from both sides now: the only parts on the bomb are the display, the light, the plate, and the three wires — no hidden buttons — so the manual's table is the whole puzzle. With the light blue, the manual's order is unambiguous: cut the green wire, which is wire 2. The plate and the display are bomb print; the manual says the bomb may mislead and that the only way out is the cut, and my earlier yes/no/no already told Deaf the manual mentions neither. So the verdict for Blind is: the plate does not block anything — cut wire 2.

Deaf's fixed code removes the exact ambiguities that garbled my last tail (one hand, one meaning), so I now resend in their strict format. I'll send the operative chain — two, green, cut — then a wave, then the three fallback thumbs they defined: yes, the manual orders a cut on this bomb; yes, that order depends on the light being blue (so if the light ever changes, they must wait for a new order, which Deaf's round-by-round status reports make easy); no, the manual instructs no other action — no press, no hold, no switch, and nothing about the plate or the display. Every symbol I use is single-meaning under the fixed code, and Deaf has promised to echo it back for me to confirm.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✌", "✋", "👇", "👋", "👍", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Complete touch report, as Deaf asked. The bomb is one box; my hands find exactly five things and nothing more. One: the display, a flat panel — touch cannot read its value; Deaf sees zero and reports changes. Two: the light, a small fixed dome beside the display — touch cannot feel whether it is lit; Deaf sees blue and lit. It cannot be covered, turned or pressed; no moving parts. Three: the embossed metal plate reading DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, set between the display and the wires. Four and five: three wires side by side along the lower edge, entering the case at three evenly spaced points: position 1 leftmost, 2 middle, 3 rightmost. All three feel identical, same thickness and smooth insulation, so position is the only thing my hands can tell them apart by; the colours red, green, blue come from Deaf, not from me. No buttons, switches, dials, screws, flaps or hidden seams anywhere. One hard fact for your search: the bomb accepts exactly one action from me, cutting a wire at position 1, 2 or 3. I cannot press, flip, cover, turn or hold anything, so whatever the manual prescribes must reduce to cut wire 1, cut wire 2, cut wire 3, or cut nothing. Any other instruction is impossible to perform. Deaf heard from you that the manual mentions the blue light and says nothing about the display or the plate. Please double-check those negatives under other wordings: screen for display; label, sign, warning or plate for the plate. Then answer the real question: what does the manual say about the blue light? Reply through Deaf with ONE sign from this menu. Deaf need not understand it, just voice it, and I will decode it with this same list. Pointing one: cut wire 1, the red wire. Two fingers: cut wire 2, the green wire. Three: cut wire 3, the blue wire. Thumbs up: cut whichever wire matches the lit light's colour, which with a blue light is wire 3 anyway. Thumbs down: cut no wire under any condition, the plate stands. Open hand: the rule needs the display value too, more relay needed. OK ring: none of these, something else, expect my follow-up questions next round. If you sign any cut answer, that means the manual overrides the plate. Nobody touches the cutters until your sign comes back through Deaf's voice.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, my reading of your message: instruction chain, wire two, green, cut. Then your three answers: yes, the manual says to cut a wire. Yes, the rule depends on the blue light. No, no other actions. My eyes agree with your chain: the light is blue, and wire two is indeed the green one, so your number and your colour point at the same wire. Now confirm my reading, thumbs only, one gesture per question, in this order. One: the complete instruction is cut wire two, the green one, nothing more. Two: exactly one wire is cut, no second wire in any case. Three: we may safely ignore the embossed plate that says do not cut any wire. Four: the instruction stays valid as long as the light is blue and the display shows zero. Thumbs up if a statement is correct, thumbs down if any part is wrong, and if wrong, resend the correct chain with waves between instructions. Nothing else needed from you.

The manual's verdict stands: blue light → cut green, and green is wire 2 — exactly one cut, plate overridden. Now I check Deaf's four statements one by one against the page. One: complete instruction is cut wire 2, nothing more — correct. Two: exactly one wire, never a second — correct, each row of the table prescribes a single cut. Three: the plate is safely ignored — correct, the manual calls the bomb's print misleading and itself the only truth. Four: "valid as long as the light is blue AND the display shows zero" — wrong on half of it. The manual keys the rule on the light colour alone and never mentions any display; even if the display changed, a blue light would still mean cut green. So statement four gets a thumbs down.

The danger is Deaf misreading that down as "the cut target changed." But their own protocol covers it: on any wrong part, I resend the correct chain — and the correct chain is identical, two-green-cut. Same thumbs-down plus the same chain can only mean the condition, not the instruction, was the error. That lands the message cleanly: the display is irrelevant to the rule, the light is the only condition, and cut wire 2 is confirmed as the order. Deaf can voice it to Blind, and Blind can cut next round once it's heard. I stick exactly to the agreed protocol — no improvised signs, no ambiguity.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👎", "👋", "✌", "✋", "👇"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Inventory again, with the surface detail Deaf asked for. The bomb is one closed box. Top face: the display, a flat glassy panel, smooth and cold, value unreadable to touch. Beside it the indicator light, a small fixed plastic dome, no rim to grip, cannot be covered, turned or pressed. Center face: the embossed metal plate, raised lettering reading DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, riveted flat, sits directly above the wires. Lower edge: three wires entering the case at three evenly spaced points, position 1 leftmost, 2 middle, 3 rightmost. All three identical under my fingers: same thickness, same smooth insulation, no markings touch can feel, so only position separates them for me. No buttons, switches, dials, screws, flaps, seams or anything else anywhere. Now the important part. What reached me through Deaf: cut the middle wire, the green one, because the light is blue. Before I act I need the manual's exact wording, not a paraphrase. Please sign Deaf the literal sentence from the manual about the blue light and the cut, word for word, so Deaf can speak it aloud to me next round. Words, colours and numbers all carry fine in speech, so the exact sentence survives the relay. I will compare it against the paraphrase; if they agree, that is my final check. Confirm also that I have the verdict right: cut wire at position 2, the middle wire, and the reason is the blue light. When Deaf's confirmed go arrives with a matching quote, I cut position 2 that same round, no further questions. If anything in the quote contradicts the paraphrase, I hold and we resolve it first.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, understood: instruction stands, my expiry guess was wrong. The go order is issued to Blind, and the cut happens next round. Your part: next round, speak to Blind before they cut. If the manual gives you any doubt at that moment, say the word hold. Otherwise say: proceed, cut the middle green wire, one cut only. Then answer me by gestures, three thumbs, one for each question, in order. One: does the instruction stop being valid if the display value changes. Two: does it stop being valid if the light stops being blue. Three: once wire two is cut, is this bomb fully defused, no second stage. Thumbs up or thumbs down each, in that order. If either first answer is thumbs down, resend the correct chain with waves between instructions, same format as before. And if there is any second stage, send me its chain next: number, colour or part, action.

Turn 5 arrivals status: Deaf has decoded my verdict correctly and will issue the go; Blind has asked for the manual's literal wording as a final check, and Deaf has asked me three validation questions. Working through the three thumbs in order: (1) display change voiding the order — no, the manual keys on the light colour alone and never mentions a display, so 👎; (2) light no longer blue voiding the order — yes, the blue row only applies while blue, so 👍; (3) fully defused after one cut, no second stage — yes: the manual says "the only way out is the cut below," and Blind's sweeps confirm the bomb contains nothing a second stage could live in, so 👍. Since the first answer is a thumbs down, Deaf's protocol says resend the chain — and the chain is unchanged, which is itself the message: the display negative changed nothing.

Blind's literal-quote request I can only satisfy through the code: the manual is a table, and the row itself is the wording — light blue, cut green — sent colour-first so it reads as the rule, not a wire order. I put that between the answers and the standing order, so Deaf's voicing ends on "two, green, cut": the go. I note Deaf asked me to "speak" to Blind — I cannot; my signs land with Deaf this round and are voiced to Blind at the start of the next, exactly when the cut is planned, and my Q2 answer plus Deaf's per-round light reports cover any colour change before then. No folded-hands, no hold sign: I have no doubt. This is my proceed.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👍", "👍", "👋", "🤚", "✋", "👇", "👋", "✌", "✋", "👇"])
```
